t: A Pacific island democracy that gained full legislative independence in 1947 while keeping the British monarch as head of state.
It broke with the United States over nuclear weapons in 1985–1987 and made its nuclear-free status law.
The Waitangi Tribunal and Treaty settlements since 1975 have reshaped relations between the Crown and Māori.
dyk: New Zealand adopted the Statute of Westminster only in 1947, sixteen years after Britain passed it, and created its own citizenship from 1 January 1949.
ev: Parliament adopts the Statute of Westminster, completing legislative independence
ANZUS Treaty signed with Australia and the United States; Legislative Council abolished
Britain joins the EEC, ending New Zealand's secure British market
Treaty of Waitangi Act creates the Waitangi Tribunal
French agents sink the Rainbow Warrior in Auckland harbour
Nuclear Free Zone Act passed; te reo Māori becomes an official language
First election under mixed-member proportional representation
Christchurch mosque shootings; most semi-automatic weapons banned
